'''Twenty One Pilots'''{{efn|Stylized in [[all lowercase]] as '''twenty one pilots''', '''twenty øne piløts''' or '''twenty {{!}} one {{!}} pilots''', and abbreviated similarly ('''tøp''' or '''TØP''')<ref name="AMbio"/>}} is an American musical duo from [[Columbus, Ohio]]. Initially a band, the group was formed in 2009 by lead vocalist [[Tyler Joseph]] along with Nick Thomas and Chris Salih, who both left in 2011. Since their departure, the line-up has consisted of Tyler Joseph and drummer [[Josh Dun]]. The duo is best known for their singles "[[Stressed Out]]", "[[Ride (Twenty One Pilots song)|Ride]]", and "[[Heathens (Twenty One Pilots song)|Heathens]]", which achieved commercial success between 2015 and 2016. The duo received a [[Grammy Award for Best Pop Duo/Group Performance]] at the [[59th Annual Grammy Awards]] for "Stressed Out".

The band independently released two albums, ''[[Twenty One Pilots (album)|Twenty One Pilots]]'' (2009) and ''[[Regional at Best]]'' (2011), before being signed by record label [[Fueled by Ramen]] in 2012. Their label debut ''[[Vessel (Twenty One Pilots album)|Vessel]]'' (2013) became the second album in history on which every track received at least a gold certification.

The duo achieved breakthrough success with their fourth album, ''[[Blurryface]]'' (2015), which produced the hit singles "Stressed Out" and "Ride" and became the first album on which every track received at least a [[RIAA certification|gold certification]] from the [[Recording Industry Association of America]]. The release of "Heathens" also made the group the first alternative artist in history to have two concurrent top five singles in the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and the third rock act in history to have two singles simultaneously chart in the top five of the ''Billboard'' Hot 100, joining [[the Beatles]] and [[Elvis Presley]].

The duo have released four more studio albums, ''[[Trench (album)|Trench]]'' (2018), ''[[Scaled and Icy]]'' (2021), ''[[Clancy (album)|Clancy]]'' (2024), and ''[[Breach (Twenty One Pilots album)|Breach]]'' (2025). They have also garnered 12 number-one songs on the [[Alternative Airplay]] chart, tying with [[Foo Fighters]] for the fifth-most.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Koltan|last=Greenwood|url=https://www.altpress.com/news/twenty-one-pliots-quickly-achieve-chart-feat/|title=Twenty One Pilots are the first to achieve this chart feat in two years.|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=May 6, 2020|access-date=March 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220401092026/https://www.altpress.com/news/twenty-one-pliots-quickly-achieve-chart-feat/|archive-date=April 1, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|first=Kevin|last=Rutherford|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/twenty-one-pilots-the-contract-number-1-alternative-airplay-1236030495/|title=Twenty One Pilots Score 12th Alternative Airplay No. 1 With 'The Contract'|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=July 25, 2025|access-date=August 19, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250725173032/https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/twenty-one-pilots-the-contract-number-1-alternative-airplay-1236030495/|archive-date=July 25, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref>

==History==

===2009–2011: Formation and self-titled album===
{{main|Twenty One Pilots (album)|l1 = ''Twenty One Pilots'' (album)}}

[[Tyler Joseph]] first met future bandmate Nick Thomas at a young age while playing youth basketball in Columbus, Ohio.<ref name="Episode 10 - Nick Thomas">{{cite web|url=https://soundcloud.com/21pilotspodcast|title=Episode 10 – Nick Thomas|website=The Twenty One Pilots Podcast|via=[[SoundCloud]]|access-date=January 19, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201031232857/https://soundcloud.com/21pilotspodcast|archive-date=October 31, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> Thomas later transferred to Joseph's middle school, and the two would remain friends throughout high school.<ref name="Billboard-2">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/artist/430557/twenty-one-pilots/biography|title=Twenty One Pilots Biography|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=March 5, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150302125816/http://www.billboard.com/artist/430557/twenty-one-pilots/biography|archive-date=March 2, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Joy-2012">{{cite news|first=Kevin|last=Joy|url=http://www.dispatch.com/content/stories/life_and_entertainment/2012/10/18/1-twenty-one-pilots-art-gn8jqp4s-1.html|title=With debut album set for release, Columbus duo Twenty One Pilots poised to break out|newspaper=[[The Columbus Dispatch]]|date=October 18, 2012|access-date=February 1, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160520151812/http://www.dispatch.com/content/stories/life_and_entertainment/2012/10/18/1-twenty-one-pilots-art-gn8jqp4s-1.html|archive-date=May 20, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Joseph began playing music after finding an old keyboard inside his closet, a Christmas gift he received from his mother, and began mimicking radio melodies.<ref>{{cite web|first=Chris|last=DeVille|url=http://www.columbusalive.com/content/blogs/sensory-overload/2012/04/interview-twenty-one-pilots-part-1.html|title=Interview: Twenty One Pilots, part 1|work=[[Columbus Alive]]|date=April 27, 2012|access-date=June 26, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714190259/http://www.columbusalive.com/content/blogs/sensory-overload/2012/04/interview-twenty-one-pilots-part-1.html|archive-date=July 14, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Messiah">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=61WpOTdThzY|title=MessiahPulse Interview: Twenty One Pilots|date=February 13, 2014 |via=YouTube|access-date=June 27, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200608074736/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=61WpOTdThzY|archive-date=June 8, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2007, Joseph released a solo EP, ''No Phun Intended'', in his parents' basement. Thomas contributed guitar to several songs on the album,<ref name="Episode 10 - Nick Thomas"/> and collaborated with Joseph on the track "Trees".<ref name="Episode 10 - Nick Thomas"/>

While attending [[Ohio State University]], Joseph met [[Texas]]-born future bandmate Chris Salih at a party. Noting the songwriter's talent and creative energy, Salih consulted Joseph about starting a band. Impressed by the recording studio Salih had built in his house, Joseph agreed to play music together and began sharing his ideas for new music. Just before their first performance, Joseph invited Thomas to join the unnamed band as a bassist. In 2009, the group moved into a house of their own, where their first album was conceptualized and recorded in the basement.<ref name="Episode 10 - Nick Thomas"/><ref name="altpress.com">{{cite magazine|first=Jordan|last=Toney|url=https://www.altpress.com/news/entry/twenty_one_pilots_chris_salih_interview_stream|title=Founding Twenty One Pilots member Chris Salih opens up about band|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=August 24, 2017|access-date=October 29, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180429070240/https://www.altpress.com/news/entry/twenty_one_pilots_chris_salih_interview_stream|archive-date=April 29, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

The band initially played for a wide variety of audiences at clubs and venues around the Columbus area. Playing at metal, hardcore, and electronic venues influenced Joseph to incorporate these disparate styles into his songwriting. To catch the attention of unfamiliar or uninterested attendees and promoters, the band began to experiment with costumes and on-stage [[acrobatics]].<ref name="altpress.com"/>

Now going by the name Twenty One Pilots,<ref name="Billboard-2"/><ref name="Joy-2012"/> the group released their debut album, ''[[Twenty One Pilots (album)|Twenty One Pilots]]'', on December 29, 2009, and began touring Ohio. Their initial marketing was grassroots; Joseph's mother would stand outside of Ohio State University, giving away tickets to their shows.<ref>{{cite web|author=Shayla D|url=https://www.inquisitr.com/3508203/twenty-one-pilots-singer-tyler-joseph-discusses-how-his-hard-work-in-basketball-paid-off-in-a-successful-music-career/|title=Twenty One Pilots Singer Tyler Joseph Discusses How His Hard Work in Basketball Paid Off in a Successful Music Career|work=[[Inquisitr]]|date=September 14, 2016|access-date=December 10, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809153122/https://www.inquisitr.com/3508203/twenty-one-pilots-singer-tyler-joseph-discusses-how-his-hard-work-in-basketball-paid-off-in-a-successful-music-career/|archive-date=August 9, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> During this time, the band participated in various "Battle of the Band" contests at The Alrosa Villa and The Basement, important Columbus music venues.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eytVsO6xi7M|title=Twenty One Pilots – Trapdoor Live @ The Battle of the Bands 10–11–09|date=November 24, 2009 |via=YouTube|access-date=February 13, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201122123429/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eytVsO6xi7M|archive-date=November 22, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ggAOfa0B2xk|title=Twenty One Pilots – Friend, Please Live @ The Battle of the Bands 10–11–09|date=November 10, 2009 |via=YouTube|access-date=February 13, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201120073504/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ggAOfa0B2xk|archive-date=November 20, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2010, the band posted two tracks to their [[SoundCloud]] account, a cover of "[[Jar of Hearts]]" by [[Christina Perri]] and "[[Con te partirò#Other cover versions|Time to Say Goodbye]]", an original song that samples "[[Con te partirò]]" by [[Andrea Bocelli]] and [[Sarah Brightman]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Jay|last=Campbell|url=http://woub.org/2012/03/14/interview-twenty-one-pilots|title=WOUB Public Media: Twenty One Pilots Interview|work=WOUB|access-date=July 30, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141020073108/http://woub.org/2012/03/14/interview-twenty-one-pilots|archive-date=October 20, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://soundcloud.com/twentonepilots|title=twentonepilots|work=SoundCloud|access-date=November 5, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160805212002/https://soundcloud.com/twentonepilots|archive-date=August 5, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> The latter track would become the first song that local drummer [[Josh Dun]] heard from the group.<ref name= "columbusalive.com">{{cite web|first=Chris|last=DeVille|url=http://www.columbusalive.com/content/blogs/sensory-overload/2012/04/interview-twenty-one-pilots-part-1.html|title=Interview with Twenty One Pilots' Tyler Joseph and Josh Dun, part 1|work=[[Columbus Alive]]|date=April 27, 2012|access-date=June 26, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714190259/http://www.columbusalive.com/content/blogs/sensory-overload/2012/04/interview-twenty-one-pilots-part-1.html|archive-date=July 14, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Joseph, Dun,<ref>{{cite web|title=Lord of Glory – New Albany Music ft. twenty one pilots| date=June 20, 2014 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tq09EEhOmsE|via=YouTube|access-date=February 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201122214050/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tq09EEhOmsE|archive-date=November 22, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=twenty one pilots interview at Five14 Church| date=June 7, 2014 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZFD5VyZpGA|via=YouTube|access-date=February 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017124237/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZFD5VyZpGA|archive-date=October 17, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=enarJ8ymhKA|title=New Albany (Feat. Tyler Joseph & Josh Dun) – Lord of Glory ( Subtítulos Español )|date=November 11, 2014 |via=YouTube|access-date=February 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022232516/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=enarJ8ymhKA|archive-date=October 22, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> and Salih participated in the musical efforts of the Columbus church Five14. They contributed to four of fourteen tracks for their album ''Clear'', with Travis Whittaker and the [[Christian rock|gospel rock band]] New Albany Music. In 2011, Joseph appeared in a three-part video called "The (Moderately Inspiring Tale of the) Longboard Rodeo Tango",<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JcQD2LXYPp0|title=The (moderately inspiring tale of the) Longboard Rodeo Tango Episode 1|date=May 21, 2014 |via=YouTube|access-date=July 27, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201120235345/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JcQD2LXYPp0|archive-date=November 20, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ILfRcBB35G8|title=The (moderately inspiring tale of the) Longboard Rodeo Tango Episode 2|date=May 21, 2014 |via=YouTube|access-date=July 27, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201118160550/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ILfRcBB35G8|archive-date=November 18, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=51dCuolxYBg|title=The (moderately inspiring tale of the) Longboard Rodeo Tango Episode 3|date=May 21, 2014 |via=YouTube|access-date=July 27, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201018064856/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=51dCuolxYBg|archive-date=October 18, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> and sang "[[O Come, O Come, Emmanuel]]" in another video, "Christmas with the Stars".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OjMAI7vDDbc|title=Tyler Joseph performs 'O come, O come, Emmanuel' at Five14 Church, OH on Christmas Eve|date=February 14, 2014 |via=YouTube|access-date=June 17, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140709165624/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OjMAI7vDDbc|archive-date=July 9, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>

===2011–2012: Lineup changes and ''Regional at Best''===
{{Main|Regional at Best|l1 = ''Regional at Best''}}
[[File:Tylerjosephtwentyonepilots.jpg|thumb|upright|Twenty One Pilots performing in 2012]]
Salih left the band on May 8, 2011, to focus on work, and Thomas left the following month on June 3 to focus on schooling, both posting farewell notes on the band's official Facebook page.<ref>{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Salih|url=https://www.facebook.com/notes/twenty-one-pilots/member-change-chris-farewell/10150231964105135 | title = Member Change: Chris' Farewell|website=Facebook|date=May 9, 2011|access-date=August 22, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190221102625/https://www.facebook.com/notes/twenty-one-pilots/member-change-chris-farewell/10150231964105135/|archive-date=February 21, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.facebook.com/notes/twenty-one-pilots/nick-thomas-farewell/10150257086085135 | title = Nick Thomas' Farewell | last = Thomas | first = Nick | date = June 3, 2011 | website = Facebook | access-date = August 22, 2016 | archive-date = November 8, 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20201108095612/https://www.facebook.com/notes/twenty-one-pilots/nick-thomas-farewell/10150257086085135/ | url-status = live }}</ref> Before departing from the project, Salih invited [[Guitar Center]] co-worker and friend of the group Josh Dun (former touring drummer for [[House of Heroes]]),<ref name="Joy-2012"/><ref>{{cite web|first=Chris|last=DeVille|url=http://www.columbusalive.com/content/blogs/sensory-overload/2012/04/interview-twenty-one-pilots-part-1.html|title=Interview: Twenty One Pilots, part 1|work=Columbusalive|date=April 27, 2012|access-date=June 26, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714190259/http://www.columbusalive.com/content/blogs/sensory-overload/2012/04/interview-twenty-one-pilots-part-1.html|archive-date=July 14, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> to take his place in the band. Impressed by the band's potential and Joseph's creative vision, Dun abandoned plans to pursue drumming in Nashville and joined the project only a few weeks before Thomas left the group.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Jordan|last=Toney|url=https://www.altpress.com/news/entry/twenty_one_pilots_chris_salih_interview_stream|title=Founding Twenty One Pilots member Chris Salih opens up about band|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=August 24, 2017|access-date=October 29, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180429070240/https://www.altpress.com/news/entry/twenty_one_pilots_chris_salih_interview_stream|archive-date=April 29, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Both Salih and Thomas remained involved with the band's production for some time after their departure.<ref name="Episode 05 - Chris Salih">{{cite web|url=https://soundcloud.com/21pilotspodcast|title=Episode 05 – Chris Salih|website=The Twenty One Pilots Podcast on SoundCloud|access-date=January 19, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201031232857/https://soundcloud.com/21pilotspodcast|archive-date=October 31, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> Thomas briefly attended school in [[North Carolina]], but moved back into Joseph and Dun's house in Columbus a year later and began to manage their [[Merchandising|merchandise]]. Thomas remained a part of the merchandise distribution crew throughout the production of ''[[Blurryface]]'' and continues to stay actively involved in the band's tour cycle.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Andy|last=Greene|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/13-things-we-learned-hanging-out-with-twenty-one-pilots-20160120|title=13 Things We Learned Hanging Out With Twenty One Pilots|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|date=January 20, 2016|access-date=February 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180623061608/https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/13-things-we-learned-hanging-out-with-twenty-one-pilots-20160120|archive-date=June 23, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Nick Thomas's Twitter account "realpootom" given on Chris Robinson's podcast|url=https://twitter.com/realPooTom?lang=en|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201228140858/https://twitter.com/realPooTom?lang=en|archive-date=December 28, 2020|access-date=February 10, 2018|publisher=Twitter}}</ref>

With a new lineup consisting of only Joseph and Dun, Twenty One Pilots self-released their second album, ''[[Regional at Best]]'', on July 8, 2011. The album was accompanied by a free CD release show on the grounds of [[New Albany High School (Ohio)|New Albany High School]]. While Salih and Thomas were involved with the conceptualization of the album, neither they nor Dun claim to have had much involvement with its production, which was handled nearly exclusively by Joseph.<ref name="Episode 05 - Chris Salih"/> The album features Joseph's brother Zack on the track "Kitchen Sink" and Joseph's college acquaintance Jocef on the track "Be Concerned".<ref>{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Roll|url=https://www.thelantern.com/2014/09/twenty-one-pilots-in-finest-form-at-hometown-show/|title=Review: Twenty One Pilots in finest form at hometown show|work=The Lantern|date=September 8, 2014|access-date=February 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201012011221/https://www.thelantern.com/2014/09/twenty-one-pilots-in-finest-form-at-hometown-show/|archive-date=October 12, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

In November 2011, after months of cultivating a fan base in the Columbus area via social media interaction and constant touring, the band played a sold-out concert at Columbus' [[Newport Music Hall]]. This caught the attention of several record labels interested in seeing if the band's appeal could stretch outside of Ohio.<ref name="Ryan G-2012">{{cite web|author=Ryan G|url=http://mezzic.com/2012/05/27/review-twenty-one-pilots-regional-at-best-2011/|title=Review twenty one pilots Regional at Best|work=Mezzic|date=May 27, 2012|access-date=February 1, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201121349/http://mezzic.com/2012/05/27/review-twenty-one-pilots-regional-at-best-2011/|archive-date=February 1, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> That same year, the duo put out two free songs via their email [[newsletter]]: the original version of "[[House of Gold (Twenty One Pilots song)|House of Gold]]" and "Two".<ref name="The site">{{cite web|url=https://www.twentyonepilots.com|title=The site|publisher=Twenty One Pilots|date=February 23, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170524030927/http://www.twentyonepilots.com/|archive-date=May 24, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=AMbio />

Joseph and Dun embarked on the Regional at Best Tour with rock band Challenger!,<ref name="Challenger! and Twenty One Pilots">{{cite web|url=http://club.kingsnake.com/index.php?/archives/1128-Challenger!-and-Twenty-One-Pilots-featured-on-The-Regional-At-Best-Tour-this-summer.html|title=Challenger! and Twenty One Pilots featured on "The Regional at Best Tour" this summer|website=Club.Kingsnake|access-date=December 28, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201026122548/http://club.kingsnake.com/index.php?%2Farchives%2F1128-Challenger%21-and-Twenty-One-Pilots-featured-on-The-Regional-At-Best-Tour-this-summer.html|archive-date=October 26, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="neufutur.com">{{cite web|first=James|last=McQuiston|url=http://neufutur.com/2011/06/the-regional-at-best-tour-featuring-challenger-and-twenty-one-pilots-kicks-off-july-16th-in-chicago-il/|title="The Regional at Best Tour" featuring Challenger! and Twenty One Pilots Kicks Off July 16th in Chicago IL!!|work=Neufutr|date=June 27, 2011|access-date=February 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200207170358/http://neufutur.com/2011/06/the-regional-at-best-tour-featuring-challenger-and-twenty-one-pilots-kicks-off-july-16th-in-chicago-il/|archive-date=February 7, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> documenting it in a series of videos uploaded to the Twenty One Pilots YouTube channel.<ref name="top40-charts.com">{{cite web|url=http://top40-charts.com/news.php?nid=68113|title='The Regional at Best Tour' Featuring Challenger! And Twenty One Pilots Kicks Off July 16th in Chicago!|work=Top40 Charts|access-date=February 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201019171116/https://top40-charts.com/news.php?nid=68113|archive-date=October 19, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

===2012–2014: Major-label signing and ''Vessel''===
{{Main|Vessel (Twenty One Pilots album)|l1 = ''Vessel'' (Twenty One Pilots album)}}

In April 2012, the band announced their signing to [[Atlantic Records]] subsidiary [[Fueled by Ramen]] during a show at the [[Express Live!|Lifestyle Communities Pavilion]].<ref name="Joy-2012" /><ref name=AMbio>{{cite web|first=Fred|last=Thomas|url=http://www.allmusic.com/artist/twenty-one-pilots-mn0002398414/biography|title=Twenty One Pilots {{!}} Biography|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=July 4, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150630165257/http://www.allmusic.com/artist/twenty-one-pilots-mn0002398414/biography|archive-date=June 30, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> On July 17, 2012, they released their debut Fueled by Ramen recording, an EP entitled ''Three Songs''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.allmusic.com/album/three-songs-mw0002486637|title=three songs – Twenty One Pilots – Release Information, Reviews and Credits|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=May 8, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160505195720/http://www.allmusic.com/album/three-songs-mw0002486637|archive-date=May 5, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|first=Matthew|last=Colwell|url=https://www.altpress.com/aptv/video/album_announcement_premiere_twenty_one_pilots_three_songs|title=Album Announcement/Video Premiere: twenty one pilots, 'three songs' EP; "Holding Onto You" live|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=June 29, 2012|access-date=February 12, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180213135147/https://www.altpress.com/aptv/video/album_announcement_premiere_twenty_one_pilots_three_songs|archive-date=February 13, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> The next month, the band embarked on a short tour with [[Neon Trees]] and [[Walk the Moon]].<ref name="Ryan G-2012" />

Joseph, in a 2023 livestream reflecting on the lead-up to what would become ''[[Vessel (Twenty One Pilots album)|Vessel]]'', talked about signing with Fueled by Ramen and ''Regional at Best'': "it was just a record that we had on the merch table when we were performing independently, and then we wanted to go record a real, professional record when we got signed – some of those songs we took from ''Regional at Best'' and kind of re-recorded them, and some of we had written new, since then. And that's what ''Vessel'' is. I know some people might not like this, but I kind of view ''Vessel'' as our first record."<ref>{{cite web|first=Emily|last=Carter|url=https://www.kerrang.com/twenty-one-pilots-vessel-tyler-joseph-josh-dun-regional-at-best|title=twenty one pilots explain the difference between their albums Vessel and Regional At Best|work=[[Kerrang!]]|date=January 9, 2023|access-date=March 16, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331094157/https://www.loudersound.com/news/twenty-one-pilots-ex-regrets-deleted-music|archive-date=March 31, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Regional at Best'' tracks "Slowtown", "Anathema", "Ruby", "Be Concerned", and "Clear" have since been made commercially unavailable.<ref>{{cite web|first=Martin|last=Kielty|url=https://www.loudersound.com/news/twenty-one-pilots-ex-regrets-deleted-music|title=Twenty One Pilots ex regrets deleted music|work=[[Metal Hammer]]|date=August 25, 2017|access-date=February 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331094157/https://www.loudersound.com/news/twenty-one-pilots-ex-regrets-deleted-music|archive-date=March 31, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref>

On November 12, 2012, the music video for "[[Holding On to You (Twenty One Pilots song)|Holding On to You]]", directed by Jordan Bahat, was released on YouTube.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ktBMxkLUIwY|title=twenty one pilots: Holding on to You|via=YouTube|date=November 14, 2012|access-date=December 1, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201213231152/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ktBMxkLUIwY|archive-date=December 13, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> On January 7 and April 19, 2013, the band released music videos for "[[Guns for Hands]]" and "[[Car Radio (song)|Car Radio]]", respectively, both directed by Mark Eshleman of Reel Bear Media.<ref name="Guns for Hands music">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Pmv8aQKO6k0|title=twenty one pilots: Guns For Hands|via=YouTube|date=January 7, 2013|access-date=December 1, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201121181950/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Pmv8aQKO6k0|archive-date=November 21, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Car Radio music">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=92XVwY54h5k|title=twenty one pilots: Car Radio|via=YouTube|date=April 19, 2013|access-date=December 1, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201213230251/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=92XVwY54h5k|archive-date=December 13, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=Lovelyitunes>{{cite web|url=https://music.apple.com/jp/album/lovely-single/634693149|title=Lovely – Single by twenty one pilots|website=[[iTunes]]|date=July 8, 2011|access-date=August 17, 2016|archive-date=September 10, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160910022641/https://itunes.apple.com/jp/album/lovely-single/id634693149|url-status=live}}</ref>

In an interview with the ''[[Huffington Post]]'', Joseph described ''Regional at Best'' as a "glorified mixtape" and confirmed that songs from that project would reappear on their major-label debut album.<ref>{{cite web|first=Glenn|last=Gamboa|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/mike-ragogna/emvesselem-chatting-with_b_2469647.html|title=Vessel : Chatting With Twenty One Pilots' Tyler Joseph, Plus Reintroducing The Johnny Stallings Arts Program and Six Market Blvd|work=[[HuffPost]]|date=January 14, 2013|access-date=February 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161218002724/http://www.huffingtonpost.com/mike-ragogna/emvesselem-chatting-with_b_2469647.html|archive-date=December 18, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> Ultimately, five tracks from ''Regional at Best'' – "[[Guns for Hands]]", "Holding On to You", "[[Ode to Sleep]]", "[[Car Radio (song)|Car Radio]]", and "Trees" – were re-recorded and released for their third album.<ref name="Vessel 10th anniversary NME">{{cite web|first=Arusa|last=Qureshi|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/twenty-one-pilots-announce-vessel-10th-anniversary-vinyl-box-set-3377383|title=Twenty One Pilots announce 'Vessel' 10th anniversary vinyl box set|work=[[NME]]|date=January 9, 2023|access-date=March 17, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240223011006/https://www.nme.com/news/music/twenty-one-pilots-announce-vessel-10th-anniversary-vinyl-box-set-3377383|archive-date=February 23, 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> "[[Lovely (Twenty One Pilots song)|Lovely]]" was also re-recorded and released as a single in Japan on April 17, 2013.<ref name="apple.com">{{cite web|url=https://music.apple.com/jp/album/lovely-single/634693149|title=Apple Music 内のTwenty One Pilots「Lovely – Single」|date=July 8, 2011|publisher=iTunes Store|access-date=June 1, 2017|archive-date=September 10, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160910022641/https://itunes.apple.com/jp/album/lovely-single/id634693149|url-status=live}}</ref><ref 2016|archive-date=September 24, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160924042025/https://itunes.apple.com/jp/album/vessel/id895278153|url-status=live}}</ref> "Glowing Eyes", "Kitchen Sink", and "Forest" appeared unchanged as bonus tracks on the UK version of ''Vessel''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.crossrhythms.co.uk/products/Twenty_One_Pilots/Vessel_Bonus_Tracks_Version/158288/|title=Twenty One Pilots – Vessel (Bonus Tracks Version)|access-date=February 12, ''Vessel'' was released on January 8, 2013,<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Mackenzie|last=Templeton|url=https://www.altpress.com/twenty-one-pilots-vessel-trivia-quiz/|title=Can you ace this twenty one No.&nbsp;21 on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]], No.&nbsp;9 on the Digital Albums chart, No.&nbsp;17 on the Internet Albums chart, No.&nbsp;15 on the Rock Albums Chart, and No.&nbsp;10 on the Alternative Albums Chart.<ref name="Digital Albums chart">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/Twenty-One-Pilots/chart-history/digital-albums/song/770347|title=Twenty One Pilots 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160920010019/http://www.billboard.com/charts/year-end/2015/top-billboard-200-albums|archive-date=September 20, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> The band's first charting single, "Holding On to You", reached No.&nbsp;10 on the ''[[Billboard charts|Billboard]]'' [[Billboard charts#Rock/Alternative|US Rock Airplay]] chart.<ref>{{cite "Guns for Hands" and "[[Lovely (Twenty One Pilots song)|Lovely]]" reached No.&nbsp;21<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard-japan.com/charts/detail?a=hot100&year=2013&month=01&day=21|title=Billboard Japan Hot 100|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=March 17, No.&nbsp;67, respectively, on the [[Japan Hot 100]].<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/twenty-one-pilots/chart-history/jpn/|title=Twenty One Pilots Billboard Japan Hot 100|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=March 17, became the second album in history to have every track receive at least a gold certification, making Twenty One Pilots the first and only band to see every song on two albums earn gold or platinum awards.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Hugh|last=McIntyre|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/hughmcintyre/2019/07/18/twenty-one-pilots-are-the-first-band-to-see-every-song-on-two-albums-earn-gold-or-platinum-awards/?sh=f41c0735953d|title=Twenty On March 17, 2014, Twenty One Pilots performed a set at the [[MTVU]] [[CheddarU|Woodie Awards]] during [[South by Southwest|SXSW]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fueledbyramen.com/news/twenty-one-pilots-perform-guns-hands-mtvu-woodie-awards-80261|title=twenty one pilots Perform 'Guns For Hands' At mtvU Woodie Awards|publisher=Fueled by Ramen|access-date=June 17, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201206130909/https://www.fueledbyramen.com/news/twenty-one-pilots-perform-guns-hands-mtvu-woodie-awards-80261|archive-date=December 6, 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref> On April 13, Twenty One Pilots performed "Car Radio" at the [[2014 MTV Movie Awards]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Lauren|last=Weigle|url=http://www.heavy.com/entertainment/2014/04/watch-twenty-one-pilots-ski-masked-performance-at-2014-mtv-movie-awards/|title=twenty one pilots live at the MTV Movie Awards 2014|work=Heavy|date=April 13, 2014|access-date=April 14, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161113065122/http://heavy.com/entertainment/2014/04/watch-twenty-one-pilots-ski-masked-performance-at-2014-mtv-movie-awards/|archive-date=November 13, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On April 28, the band performed "Car Radio" on ''[[Late Night with Seth Meyers]]''.<ref>{{cite web|first=Michele|last=Bird|url=http://www.altpress.com/news/entry/watch_twenty_one_pilots_perform_car_radio_on_late_night_with_seth_meyers|title=Watch twenty one pilots perform 'Car Radio' on 'Late Night With Seth Meyers'|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=April 29, 2014|access-date=July 31, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160802215240/http://www.altpress.com/news/entry/watch_twenty_one_pilots_perform_car_radio_on_late_night_with_seth_meyers|archive-date=August 2, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2014, Twenty One Pilots played a number of music festivals and other events around the United States, such as [[Lollapalooza]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lollapalooza.com/2013-artist/twenty-one-pilots/|title=Twenty One Pilots|website=Lollapalooza.com|access-date=June 17, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140715002318/http://www.lollapalooza.com/2013-artist/twenty-one-pilots/|archive-date=July 15, 2014}}</ref> [[Bonnaroo]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lineup.bonnaroo.com/past/2013/band/twenty-|title=Twenty One Pilots|website=Bonnaroo.com|access-date=June 17, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140617233010/http://lineup.bonnaroo.com/past/2013/band/twenty-|archive-date=June 17, 2014}}</ref> [[Boston Calling Music Festival|Boston Calling]], and [[Firefly Music Festival|Firefly]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.twentyonepilots.com/news/firefly-music-festival|title=Firefly Music Festival|website=Twentyonepilots.com|access-date=June 17, 2014|archive-date=July 14, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714203051/http://www.twentyonepilots.com/news/firefly-music-festival|url-status=live}}</ref> Requests from many of these cities were incorporated into the band's first headlining tour, the [[Quiet Is Violent World Tour]], which began in September 2014 and ended in November of the same year.<ref name="self tour">{{cite web|url=http://www.twentyonepilots.com/tour|title=Tour|website=Twentyonepilots.com|access-date=June 17, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141003130920/http://twentyonepilots.com/tour|archive-date=October 3, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On December 31, 2014, the band released a music video for "Ode to Sleep". Composed of footage captured by the band's creative director Mark Eshleman from three concerts over the preceding three years, the video depicted the band's growth from their origins as a small local band to a nationally popular alternative act.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=How Twenty One Pilots' Tyler Joseph Captured Their Career on Film for 'Ode to Sleep'|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/magazine-feature/7325453/twenty-one-pilots-ode-to-sleep-video-history|magazine=Billboard|date=April 7, 2016|access-date=February 13, 2018|archive-date=November 28, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201128050525/https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/magazine-feature/7325453/twenty-one-pilots-ode-to-sleep-video-history|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Haskoor|first1=Michael|title=Watch Twenty One Pilots' Music Video for 'Ode to Sleep,' Three Years in the Making Read More: Watch Twenty One Pilots' Music Video for 'Ode to Sleep'|url=http://diffuser.fm/twenty-one-pilots-ode-to-sleep-music-video/|website=Diffuser.fm|date=January 2, 2015 |publisher=Loudwire Network|access-date=January 5, 2015|archive-date=December 18, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161218131134/http://diffuser.fm/twenty-one-pilots-ode-to-sleep-music-video/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== 2015–2017: ''Blurryface'' and commercial success ===
{{Main|Blurryface|l1 = ''Blurryface''}}

On March 16, 2015, the band announced that a new album, ''[[Blurryface]]'', was to be released on May 19.<ref name="AP Fairly Local">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.altpress.com/hear_twenty_one_pilots_eerie_new_single_fairly_local_from_impending_album_b/|title=Hear twenty one pilots' eerie new single "Fairly Local" from impending album 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="idobi tour">{{cite web|first=Hannah|last=Pierangelo|url=http://idobi.com/news/2015/03/twenty-one-pilots-announce-new-album-tour-dates/|title=Twenty One Pilots Announce New Album + Tour Dates|work=Idobi|date=March 17, 2015|access-date=February 2, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160502132451/http://idobi.com/news/2015/03/twenty-one-pilots-announce-new-album-tour-dates/|archive-date=May 2, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> They released the first single, "[[Fairly Local]]", on March 17.<ref name="AP Fairly Local"/> Their second single of the album, "[[Tear in My Heart]]", and its music video were released on April 5, 2015.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Brian|last=Kraus|url=http://www.altpress.com/news/entry/twenty_one_pilots_tear_in_my_heart|title=twenty one pilots release video for exuberant new single, "Tear in My Heart"|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=April 6, 2015|access-date=July 1, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180712052917/https://www.altpress.com/news/entry/twenty_one_pilots_tear_in_my_heart|archive-date=July 12, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> On April 28, "[[Stressed Out]]", the third song released from the album, was released along with a music video.<ref>{{cite web|first=Brenna|last=Ehrlich|url=https://www.mtv.com/news/w8iwka/twenty-one-pilots-blurry-face-stressed-out-video|title=Um, Why Is The Dude From Twenty One Pilots Covered In Black 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201132948/https://www.mtv.com/news/w8iwka/twenty-one-pilots-blurry-face-stressed-out-video|archive-date=December 1, 2022|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.altpress.com/news/entry/twenty_one_pilots_long_for_the_good_old_days_in_somber_stressed_out_video|title=twenty one pilots long for 'the 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Courtney|last=Smith|url=http://radio.com/2015/04/28/twenty-one-pilots-stressed-out-video/|title=Twenty One Pilots' 'Stressed Out' Video Puts on a Suburban Fairytale: Watch|work=[[Audacy|Radio.com]]|date=April 28, 2015|access-date=April 29, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518083528/http://radio.com/2015/04/28/twenty-one-pilots-stressed-out-video/|archive-date=May 18, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> "Stressed Out" became the group's best-selling single, having been certified 13× Platinum, and peaking at No. 2 on the U.S. [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], and No. 1 on both the [[Alternative Songs]] and [[List of number-one Billboard Rock Songs|Hot Rock Songs]] charts, while also surpassing over 2.8&nbsp;billion views on YouTube.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Gary|last=Trust|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/justin-bieber-no-1-hot-100-love-yourself/|title=Justin Bieber Retakes No. 1 Spot From Zayn on Hot 100|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=February 16, 2016|access-date=February 16, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|first=Maggie|last=Dickman|url=http://www.altpress.com/news/entry/twenty_one_pilots_stressed_out_music_video_one_billion_views_youtube|title=Twenty One Pilots 'Stressed Out' music video has surpassed one billion views on YouTube|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=June 23, 2017|access-date=September 17, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180712052039/https://www.altpress.com/news/entry/twenty_one_pilots_stressed_out_music_video_one_billion_views_youtube|archive-date=July 12, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

''Blurryface'' was released two days early on May 17, 2015, and sold 134,000 copies in the first week in the U.S. which made it the band's first No. 1 album on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]].<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Keith|last=Caulfield|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/twenty-one-pilots-first-no-1-album-billboard-200/|title=Twenty One Pilots Earn First No. 1 Album on Billboard 200 Chart|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=May 27, 2015|access-date=November 4, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160623154824/http://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/chart-beat/6576138/twenty-one-pilots-first-no-1-album-billboard-200|archive-date=June 23, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> On May 22, 2016, ''Blurryface'' won in the category of "Top Rock Album" at the [[Billboard Music Award|''Billboard'' Music Awards]], while the band won the category of "Top Rock Artist".<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/bbma/7378353/billboard-music-awards-2016-complete-winners-list|title=Billboard Music Awards 2016: Complete Winners List|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=May 22, 2016|access-date=May 24, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200304192110/https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/bbma/7378353/billboard-music-awards-2016-complete-winners-list|archive-date=March 4, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Blurryface'' became the first album on which every track received at least a [[RIAA certification|gold certification]] from the [[Recording Industry Association of America]].<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Chris|last=Payne|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/twenty-one-pilots-blurryface-every-song-riaa-gold-8223671/|title=Twenty One Pilots' 'Blurryface' Becomes First Album With Every Song RIAA-Certified Gold|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=March 1, 2018|access-date=March 1, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201120212125/https://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/rock/8223671/twenty-one-pilots-blurryface-every-song-riaa-gold/|archive-date=November 20, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.riaa.com/twenty-one-pilots-blurryface-earns-unrivaled-gold-platinum-achievement-first-album-digital-era-every-song-riaa-certified/|title=Twenty One Pilots' 'Blurryface' Earns The band began the Blurryface Tour on May 11, 2015, in [[Glasgow]], Scotland. Their headline route spanned the United States, England, and Canada.<ref>{{cite web|first=Sarah|last=Pittman|url=https://news.pollstar.com/2015/03/17/twenty-one-pilots-lock-down-2015-world-tour/|title=Twenty One Pilots Lock Down 2015 World Tour|work=Pollarstar|date=March 17, 2015|access-date=March 20, 2024}}</ref> The U.S. leg began September 8, 2015, and featured [[Echosmith]] and [[Finish Ticket]] as openers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.axs.com/twenty-one-pilots-reveal-tour-dates-for-the-fall-of-2015-45124|title=Twenty One Pilots reveal tour dates for the fall of 2015|work=AXS|first=Natalie|last=Kuchik|access-date=May 31, 2016|date=March 20, 2015|archive-date=June 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160609034316/http://www.axs.com/twenty-one-pilots-reveal-tour-dates-for-the-fall-of-2015-45124|url-status=live}}</ref> Twenty One Pilots performed "Stressed Out" on ''Late Night with Seth Meyers'' on September 14, 2015.<ref>{{cite web|first=Caryn|last=Robbins|url=http://www.broadwayworld.com/bwwtv/article/VIDEO-Twenty-One-Pilots-Perform-New-Single-Stressed-Out-on-LATE-NIGHT-20150915|title=Twenty One Pilots Perform New Single 'Stressed Out' on Late Night|work=[[BroadwayWorld]]|date=September 15, 2015|access-date=January 21, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305044145/http://www.broadwayworld.com/bwwtv/article/VIDEO-Twenty-One-Pilots-Perform-New-Single-Stressed-Out-on-LATE-NIGHT-20150915|archive-date=March 5, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> The band announced a London show in February 2016, and later announced a run of UK dates, with a second London date added. The band [[Transviolet]] served as openers.<ref>{{cite web|first=Emily|last=Carter|url=http://www.kerrang.com/35188/twenty-one-pilots-announce-huge-uk-tour-including-second-london-date/|title=twenty one pilots Announce Huge UK Tour – Including Second London Date|work=[[Kerrang!]]|date=September 1, 2015|access-date=November 30, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161201080704/http://www.kerrang.com/35188/twenty-one-pilots-announce-huge-uk-tour-including-second-london-date/|archive-date=December 1, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On June 16, 2016, the band released the song "[[Heathens (Twenty One Pilots song)|Heathens]]" as the first single from the ''[[Suicide Squad (2016 film)|Suicide Squad]]'' soundtrack, earlier than the expected release date of June 24, after the song leaked onto the internet on June 15.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thenextweb.com/insider/2016/08/03/atlantic-records-wants-reddit-snitch-redditor-leaked-track-suicide-squad-score/#gref|title=Record label wants Reddit to snitch on the user that leaked Suicide Squad soundtrack|date=August 3, 2016|access-date=August 5, 2016|archive-date=December 6, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201206174759/https://thenextweb.com/insider/2016/08/03/atlantic-records-wants-reddit-snitch-redditor-leaked-track-suicide-squad-score/#gref|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Mazin|last=Sidahmed|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2016/aug/04/atlantic-records-reddit-ip-address-suicide-squad-leak|title=Atlantic Records asks Reddit for user's IP address over Suicide Squad song leak|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=August 4, 2016|access-date=August 5, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170105103547/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2016/aug/04/atlantic-records-reddit-ip-address-suicide-squad-leak|archive-date=January 5, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Daniel|last=Van Boom|url=http://www.cnet.com/news/suicide-squad-twenty-one-pilots-song-leak-reddit-has-answers-record-label-says/|title=Who leaked that 'Suicide Squad' song? Joseph and Dun collaborated with [[Mutemath]] again for a five-song EP, ''TOPxMM'', composed of remixes and re-imaginings of four tracks from ''Blurryface'' as well as "Heathens". The EP was uploaded onto the band's official website free of charge on December 19; a 25-minute long video of the bands recording the songs live in studio was also released on the band's YouTube channel.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.altpress.com/watch_twenty_one_pilots_mutemath_sessions_download_free_ep/|title=Twenty One Pilots open up on EP with Mutemath—"We had a blast doing it"|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=December 20, 2016|access-date=March 21, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221106140019/https://www.altpress.com/watch_twenty_one_pilots_mutemath_sessions_download_free_ep/|archive-date=November 6, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|first=Colin|last=Stutz|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/twenty-one-pilots-mutemath-5-songs-live-video-download-7625663/|title=Twenty One Pilots Reimagine 5 Songs With Mutemath for Live Video, Free EP: Watch|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=December 19, 2016|access-date=March 21, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230715235831/https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/twenty-one-pilots-mutemath-5-songs-live-video-download-7625663/|archive-date=July 15, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kerrang.com/watch-t%C3%B8p-team-up-with-mutemath-for-amazing-live-session|title=Watch TØP Team Up With Mutemath For Amazing Live Session|work=[[Kerrang!]]|date=December 20, 2016|access-date=March 21, 2024}}</ref>

On February 12, 2017, Twenty One Pilots won a [[Grammy Award]] for "Stressed Out" in the [[Grammy Award for Best Pop Duo/Group Performance|Best Pop Duo/Group Performance]] category. The band stripped to their underwear before taking the stage, with Joseph claiming in their acceptance speech that this was a fulfillment of a promise the duo had made each other in their early days as a local Columbus band.<ref name="Grammy59">{{cite web|url=http://www.grammy.com/nominees|title=59th Annual Grammy Awards Nominees|work=The Recording Academy|access-date=December 6, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120503164723/http://www.grammy.com/nominees|archive-date=May 3, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|first=Lyndsey|last=Havens|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/grammys/7686280/twenty-one-pilots-pants-grammys-2017|title=Twenty One Pilots Drop Their Pants To Accept Grammy Award (For a Legitimate Reason)|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=February 13, 2017|access-date=October 16, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201208222824/https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/grammys/7686280/twenty-one-pilots-pants-grammys-2017|archive-date=December 8, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/music/2017/02/12/winners-list-who-won-what-59th-annual-grammys/97737914/|title=Grammys 2017: The complete list of winners|work=[[USA Today]]|date=February 12, 2017|access-date=October 16, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201029083804/https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/music/2017/02/12/winners-list-who-won-what-59th-annual-grammys/97737914/|archive-date=October 29, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

On March 27, 2017, the band began selling tickets for Tour De Columbus, a five-date hometown tour taking place in June 2017.<ref name="ABC6">{{cite web|first=Csaba|last=Sukosd|url=http://abc6onyourside.com/news/local/twenty-one-pilots-adds-5th-columbus-show-at-nationwide-arena|title=Twenty One Pilots adds 5th Columbus show at Nationwide Arena|publisher=WSYX|date=March 30, 2017|access-date=May 11, 2017|agency=ABC6|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170612220311/http://abc6onyourside.com/news/local/twenty-one-pilots-adds-5th-columbus-show-at-nationwide-arena|archive-date=June 12, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> The duo performed at several small venues they first played as a local band including The Basement, [[Newport Music Hall]], and [[Express Live!]], before ending their tour cycle with arena shows at [[Nationwide Arena]] and [[Value City Arena]].<ref name="Columbus Dispatch">{{cite news|first=Terry|last=Mikesell|url=http://www.dispatch.com/entertainmentlife/20170327/twenty-one-pilots-using-lottery-for-tickets-to-three-columbus-shows-in-smaller-venues|title=Twenty One Pilots using lottery for tickets to three Columbus shows in smaller venues|newspaper=[[The Columbus Dispatch]]|date=March 29, 2017|access-date=May 11, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170330043138/http://www.dispatch.com/entertainmentlife/20170327/twenty-one-pilots-using-lottery-for-tickets-to-three-columbus-shows-in-smaller-venues|archive-date=March 30, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In an interview with ''[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]'' in November 2016, Twenty One Pilots stated that after their last show for ''Blurryface'', they will be "going dark" to focus on new music. Joseph stated that he would like to focus on lyrical content of the music, and bring the music back to the "authenticity, lyrics, delivery, and fearlessness of songwriting" similar to that of their self-titled debut album.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Mackenzie|last=Hall|url=http://www.altpress.com/news/entry/twenty_one_pilots_issue_342|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|title=Twenty One Pilots talk new music, fans, more in our latest issue|date=November 21, 2016|access-date=June 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107113625/https://www.altpress.com/news/entry/twenty_one_pilots_issue_342|archive-date=November 7, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> The band's last activity came in July 2017 in the form of posts on social media depicting an eye closing over lyrics from several of their songs.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Maggie|last=Dickman|url=https://www.altpress.com/news/entry/twenty_one_pilots_tease_come_and_find_me|title=Update: Twenty One Pilots tease "come and find me," and fans are freaking out|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=July 7, 2017|access-date=February 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180211072258/https://www.altpress.com/news/entry/twenty_one_pilots_tease_come_and_find_me|archive-date=February 11, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Benjamin|url=https://www.fuse.tv/2017/07/twenty-one-pilots-youll-have-to-come-find-me-tease-lyrics|title=Twenty One Pilots Are Teasing Something & Fans Are Going Nuts|work=[[Fuse (TV channel)|Fuse]]|date=July 7, 2017|access-date=February 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180211071926/https://www.fuse.tv/2017/07/twenty-one-pilots-youll-have-to-come-find-me-tease-lyrics|archive-date=February 11, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In March 2018, their song "[[Hometown (Twenty One Pilots song)|Hometown]]" received a [[RIAA certification|gold certification]] from the [[Recording Industry Association of America|RIAA]], making ''Blurryface'' the first full-length album to have every track achieve at least gold certification.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Hugh|last=McIntyre|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/hughmcintyre/2018/03/01/twenty-one-pilots-blurryface-is-the-first-album-in-history-to-earn-this-golden-distinction/|title=Twenty One Pilots' 'Blurryface' Is The First Album in History To Earn This Golden Distinction|magazine=[[Forbes]]|date=March 1, 2018|access-date=April 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180423102529/https://www.forbes.com/sites/hughmcintyre/2018/03/01/twenty-one-pilots-blurryface-is-the-first-album-in-history-to-earn-this-golden-distinction/|archive-date=April 23, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.riaa.com/twenty-one-pilots-blurryface-earns-unrivaled-gold-platinum-achievement-first-album-digital-era-every-song-riaa-certified/|title=Twenty One Pilots' "Blurryface" Earns Unrivaled Gold & Platinum Achievement: First Album In Digital Era With Every Song RIAA Certified – RIAA|work=[[Recording Industry Association of America|RIAA]]|date=March 1, 2018|access-date=April 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201228140905/https://www.riaa.com/twenty-one-pilots-blurryface-earns-unrivaled-gold-platinum-achievement-first-album-digital-era-every-song-riaa-certified/|archive-date=December 28, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

===2018–2020: ''Trench''===
{{Main|Trench (album)|l1 = ''Trench'' (album)}}

In April 2018, a cryptic message was uncovered on the band's web store, which revealed a website known as ''dmaorg.info''. Fans began using clues and found other sections of this site, hinting at the possibility of the band's return. There were multiple images uploaded to the website, including letters from a character named "Clancy".<ref>{{cite web|first=Woodrow|last=Whyte|url=https://www.popbuzz.com/music/artists/twenty-one-pilots/theories-newsletter-clancy-dema/|title=Twenty One Pilots' billboards popped up in London over 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> In July 2018, Twenty One Pilots broke their year-long silence, first sending a cryptic email to fans and later posting a video to all social media platforms and updating their logo and branding.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Whitney|last=Shoemaker|url=https://www.altpress.com/news/twenty-one-pilots-break-social-media-silence/|title=Twenty One Pilots Just Broke Their Social Media Silence With Cryptic Post|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=July 9, 2018|access-date=July 9, magazine|first=Alessandra|last=Rincón|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/5-things-we-want-from-twenty-one-pilots-new-album-8464282/|title=5 Things We Want From Twenty One Pilots' New Columbus, Ohio, in which he spoke about the band's year-long hiatus, creating the new album, and battling against personal demons and insecurities.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=twentyonepilots On October 16, the band embarked on their worldwide Bandito Tour, starting in the U.S. and continuing with legs in Oceania and Europe.<ref name="The Bandito Tour">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.altpress.com/news/twenty-one-pilots-announce-the-bandito-tour-2018/|title=Twenty One Pilots announce the 'Bandito' tour|date=July 11, 2018|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|access-date=October 10, 2018|archive-date=July 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180711204747/https://www.altpress.com/news/twenty-one-pilots-announce-the-bandito-tour-2018/|url-status=live}}</ref> They also announced additional 2019 tour dates for shows in Canada, Mexico and the U.S.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Philip|last=Trapp|url=https://www.altpress.com/news/twenty-one-pilots-bandito-tour-new-dates/|title=Twenty One Pilots Add New Bandito Tour Dates|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=October 2, 2018|access-date=November 3, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201228140953/https://www.altpress.com/news/twenty-one-pilots-bandito-tour-new-dates/|archive-date=December 28, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> The band's stunts during the set included leaping, backflipping, vertical crowd-surfing, suspended bridge walking, and scaffolding scaling.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Gab|last=Ginsberg|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/twenty-one-pilots-bandito-tour-recap-nyc-show-8482624/|title=6 Twenty One Pilots Stunts That Make The Bandito Tour a Must-See|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=October 31, 2018|access-date=November 3, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201228140951/https://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/rock/8482624/twenty-one-pilots-bandito-tour-recap-nyc-show|archive-date=December 28, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Twenty One Pilots Resorts World Arena, Birmingham 2019.jpg|thumb|left|Twenty One Pilots performing at [[Resorts World Arena]], Birmingham in 2019]]

On January 22, 2019, the music video for "[[Chlorine (Twenty One Pilots song)|Chlorine]]" was unveiled upon the song's release as a single and was directed by Mark Eshleman of Reel Bear Media, featuring an alien-like creature named "Ned".<ref>{{cite AV media|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eJnQBXmZ7Ek|title=twenty one pilots – Chlorine (Official Video)|date=January 22, 2019|access-date=January 26, 2019|via=YouTube|archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211030/eJnQBXmZ7Ek|archive-date=October 30, 2021}}{{cbignore}}</ref> The band headlined a number of festivals in the summer of 2019, including [[Reading and Leeds Festivals|Reading and Leeds]] and Lollapalooza.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rocksound.tv/news/read/reading-leeds-festival-headliners-2019-twenty-one-pilots/|title=Twenty One Pilots Are Headlining Reading and Leeds|magazine=[[Rock Sound]]|access-date=March 21, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201228140945/https://www.rocksound.tv/news/read/reading-leeds-festival-headliners-2019-twenty-one-pilots|archive-date=December 28, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/lollapalooza-2019-ariana-grande-childish-gambino-tame-impala-strokes-lineup-810580/|title=Lollapalooza 2019: Ariana Grande, Childish Gambino, Tame Impala, Strokes to Headline|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|date=March 20, 2019|access-date=March 21, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190321015121/https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/lollapalooza-2019-ariana-grande-childish-gambino-tame-impala-strokes-lineup-810580/|archive-date=March 21, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

On March 4, 2019, the band confirmed that they were working on their next studio album.<ref>{{cite web|first=Gary|last=Ryan|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/twenty-one-pilots-reveal-details-next-album-theres-definitely-end-game-2456640|title=Twenty One Pilots reveal details of next album: "There's definitely an end-game"|work=[[NME]]|date=March 4, 2019|access-date=April 7, 2021}}</ref> About the possible theme, Joseph said, "there's a character that hasn't been talked about on any record yet that plays a huge role in the narrative that obviously will need to be talked about and it's probably where we're going next".<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Gil|last=Kaufman|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/twenty-one-pilots-tease-end-blurryface-story-8501154/|title=Twenty One Pilots Tease 'End Game' to 'Blurryface' Saga in New Interview|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=March 5, 2019|access-date=April 7, 2021}}</ref>

On June 19, 2019, a re-imagined version of "Chlorine", titled "Chlorine (19.4326° N, 99.1332° W)", was released. It was the first song to be released from the ''Location Sessions'' extended play. Other songs in the series include "Cut My Lip (Brooklyn)" and "The Hype (Berlin)".{{Efn|"Chlorine (19.4326° N, 99.1332° W)" was later retitled to "Chlorine (Mexico City)", and "Cut My Lip (Brooklyn)" was formally titled "Cut My Lip (40.6782°N, 73.9442° W)".}}<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.altpress.com/news/twenty-one-pilots-tyler-joseph-reconstructed-live-performance/|title=Twenty One Pilots tracks reconstructed by Tyler Joseph for special|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=June 28, 2019|access-date=June 29, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201228140959/https://www.altpress.com/news/twenty-one-pilots-tyler-joseph-reconstructed-live-performance/|archive-date=December 28, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.grammy.com/grammys/news/twenty-one-pilots-release-re-imagined-chlorine%C2%A0194326%C2%B0-n-991332%C2%B0-w|title=Twenty One Pilots Release Re-Imagined "Chlorine (19.4326° N, 99.1332° W)"|date=April 30, 2017|access-date=June 29, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201228141001/https://www.grammy.com/grammys/news/twenty-one-pilots-release-re-imagined-chlorine%C2%A0194326%C2%B0-n-991332%C2%B0-w|archive-date=December 28, 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2019, Nationwide Boulevard in Columbus, Ohio was temporarily renamed to Twenty One Pilots Boulevard to celebrate two hometown shows at the Nationwide Arena in Columbus, where the band also opened up a pop-up shop named "Ned's Bayou", with both the name of the shop and the merch being based on the character that appeared in the music video for "Chlorine".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dontboreus.thebrag.com/twenty-one-pilots-street-hometown/|title=Twenty One Pilots have had a street named after them in their hometown|date=June 26, 2019|access-date=June 29, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201228140945/https://dontboreus.thebrag.com/twenty-one-pilots-street-hometown/|archive-date=December 28, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> On July 16, 2019, "[[The Hype (Twenty One Pilots song)|The Hype]]" was sent to US alternative radio as the sixth and final single from ''Trench''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.allaccess.com/alternative/future-releases|title=The Hype single release|access-date=July 9, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180729053929/https://www.allaccess.com/alternative/future-releases|archive-date=July 29, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

On April 9, 2020, the duo released the song "[[Level of Concern]]", which marked the first musical output by the duo since the release of ''Trench''.<ref>{{cite web|first=Alex|last=Young|url=https://consequence.net/2020/04/twenty-one-pilots-reveal-new-single-level-of-concern-stream/|title=Twenty One Pilots Reveal New Single "Level of Concern": Stream|work=[[Consequence (publication)|Consequence]]|date=April 9, 2020|access-date=April 10, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200410114230/https://consequence.net/2020/04/twenty-one-pilots-reveal-new-single-level-of-concern-stream/|archive-date=April 10, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine|first=Chris|last=Payne|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/twenty-one-pilots-level-concern-video-9354939/|title=Twenty One Pilots Take on the Quarantine Blues With 'Level of Concern': Watch|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=April 9, 2020|access-date=April 10, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200410124703/https://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/rock/9354939/twenty-one-pilots-level-concern-video|archive-date=April 10, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> "Level of Concern" references [[COVID-19 pandemic]]-induced anxiety, and its accompanying music video was filmed in Joseph and Dun's homes while they were under [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] due to the pandemic. Joseph directed a portion of the song's proceeds to Crew Nation, a charity for live music crews who could not be paid during the lockdowns.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=tylerrjoseph |number=1246939889419116544 |title=i also want a portion of whatever money this song makes to go to this charity i saw called crew nation. it provides funding for people who work in the live music industry who don’t have a job right now. http://livenation.com/CrewNation |date=April 5, 2020 |access-date=April 9, 2020 |link=https://twitter.com/tylerrjoseph/status/1246939889419116544 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200411193444/https://twitter.com/tylerrjoseph/status/1246939889419116544 |archive-date=April 11, 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref>

The duo later posted a video in June, as well as a photo with the code "LOC-491-555-09JKL", which could be typed into the band's website to unlock the first of 20 "USB drives" which were later revealed to be part of a scavenger hunt based around "Level of Concern."<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.altpress.com/twenty-one-pilots-coded-website-hunt/|title=twenty one pilots send fans on a scavenger hunt with a cryptic website|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=June 12, 2020|access-date=September 5, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240627144334/https://www.altpress.com/twenty-one-pilots-coded-website-hunt/|archive-date=June 27, 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> The ultimate reward for the scavenger hunt was exclusive digital content featured in all 20 zip drives, a video of Joseph congratulating fans for completing the scavenger hunt, and a spot in their cryptic "Never-Ending" music video for "Level of Concern", which earned a Guinness World Record for the longest run for a music video, having streamed from June 21 to December 16 (177 days), beating the previous record set by producer [[Pharrell Williams]] (24 hours).<ref>{{cite web|first=Leah|last=Asmelash|url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/12/23/entertainment/twenty-one-pilots-music-video-record-trnd|title=This is the longest music video of all time – and it would take you more than 4,200 hours to watch|website=[[CNN]]|date=December 28, 2020|access-date=September 5, 2025|archive-url=https://archive.today/20250905223528/https://www.cnn.com/2020/12/23/entertainment/twenty-one-pilots-music-video-record-trnd|archive-date=September 5, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref>

In November 2020, Dun revealed that the duo were still working "remotely" on their next album, with both members being in different locations due to the lockdown. He described the recording process: "we both have our own studios, which is really nice, so he comes up with a lot of stuff at his studio, sends it over to me, and then I come up with some stuff here at my studio and then send it back".<ref>{{cite web|first=Emily|last=Carter|url=https://www.kerrang.com/the-news/tyler-joseph-confirms-hes-currently-working-on-the-new-twenty-one-pilots-album/|title=Tyler Joseph Confirms twenty one pilots Are Working On Their New Album|magazine=[[Kerrang!]]|date=November 13, 2020|access-date=April 7, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230421085815/https://www.kerrang.com/tyler-joseph-confirms-hes-currently-working-on-the-new-twenty-one-pilots-album|archive-date=April 21, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> On December 8, 2020, the band released a Christmas single, "[[Christmas Saves the Year]]", following a [[Twitch.tv|Twitch]] stream by Joseph.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Rachel|last=Campbell|url=https://www.altpress.com/news/twenty-one-pilots-christmas-saves-the-year-song/|title=Hear Twenty One Pilots' surprise holiday song "Christmas Saves The Year"|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=December 8, 2020|access-date=December 8, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201209020322/https://www.altpress.com/news/twenty-one-pilots-christmas-saves-the-year-song/|archive-date=December 9, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== 2021–2023: ''Scaled and Icy'' ===
{{Main|Scaled and Icy|l1 = ''Scaled and Icy''}}
[[File:Twenty One Pilots in Denver - September 25, 2021.jpg|thumb|right|Twenty One Pilots performing during the [[Takeover Tour]] in September 2021]]

The duo's sixth studio album, ''[[Scaled and Icy]]'', was released on May 21, 2021.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Gil|last=Kaufman|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/twenty-one-pilots-new-album-scaled-and-icy-livestream-concert-9552656/|title=Twenty One Pilots Announce New Album 'Scaled and Icy' & a Livestream Concert|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=April 7, 2021|access-date=March 6, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240205073229/https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/twenty-one-pilots-new-album-scaled-and-icy-livestream-concert-9552656/|archive-date=February 5, 2024|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|first=Claire|last=Shaffer|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/twenty-one-pilots-scaled-and-icy-shy-away-1151971/|title=Twenty One Pilots Preview New Album 'Scaled and Icy' With First Single 'Shy Away'|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|date=April 7, 2021|access-date=March 6, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240203182836/https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/twenty-one-pilots-scaled-and-icy-shy-away-1151971/|archive-date=February 3, 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> The album's name is an [[anagram]], which spells out "Clancy is dead", and is a play on the phrase "scaled back and isolated", due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Ali|last=Shutler|url=https://www.altpress.com/twenty-one-pilots-lyrics-hidden-meanings/|title=10 hidden meanings in twenty one pilots lyrics you probably didn't know|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=March 18, 2022|access-date=March 6, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231227181929/https://www.altpress.com/twenty-one-pilots-lyrics-hidden-meanings/|archive-date=December 27, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> The album was first teased on April 6, 2021, through ''dmaorg.info'' via a poster that included the text "New Album ''and'' Livestream Experience". The album was officially announced by the band the following day, alongside the release of its lead single, "[[Shy Away]]".<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Daniel|last=Kohn|url=https://www.spin.com/2021/04/twenty-one-pilots-announce-new-album-scaled-and-icy-share-shy-away/|title=Twenty One Pilots Announce New Album Scaled And Icy, Share 'Shy Away'|magazine=[[Spin (magazine)|Spin]]|date=April 7, 2021|access-date=March 6, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231202132205/https://www.spin.com/2021/04/twenty-one-pilots-announce-new-album-scaled-and-icy-share-shy-away/|archive-date=December 2, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> The second single from the album, "[[Choker (song)|Choker]]", was released on April 30, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Reilly|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/twenty-one-pilots-to-debut-new-single-choker-at-special-fan-event-2930485|title=Twenty One Pilots to debut new single 'Choker' at special fan event|work=[[NME]]|date=April 29, 2021|access-date=March 6, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230326032300/https://www.nme.com/news/music/twenty-one-pilots-to-debut-new-single-choker-at-special-fan-event-2930485|archive-date=March 26, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> The third single from the album, "[[Saturday (twenty one pilots song)|Saturday]]", was released on May 18, 2021;<ref>{{cite web|first=Emily|last=Carter|url=https://www.kerrang.com/the-news/twenty-one-pilots-released-a-brand-new-song-saturday/|title=twenty one pilots get their dancing shoes on for new single Saturday|work=[[Kerrang!]]|date=May 18, 2021|access-date=March 6, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210601034918/https://www.kerrang.com/the-news/twenty-one-pilots-released-a-brand-new-song-saturday/|archive-date=June 1, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> its music video followed on July 8.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Hannah|last=Dailey|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/pop/twenty-one-pilots-saturday-video-9598262/|title=A Sea Monster Crashes Twenty One Pilots' Aquatic 'Saturday' Video: Watch|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=July 8, 2021|access-date=March 6, Two days before the release of "Shy Away", the band announced a livestream concert to take place on May 21, 2021, coinciding with the album's release. The livestream, described as being "career-spanning", was held at [[Value City Arena]] and included live performances of songs from ''Scaled and Icy'', as well as previous records.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Gil|last=Kaufman|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/twenty-one-pilots-new-album-scaled-and-icy-livestream-concert-9552656/|title=Twenty One Pilots Announce New Album 'Scaled and 2024|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|first=Chris|last=Willman|url=https://variety.com/2021/music/news/twenty-one-pilots-new-album-may-livestream-1234945895/|title=Twenty One Pilots Debuts The show also introduced a new live touring band that would join the duo for future shows.<ref name="Billboard">{{cite magazine|first=Gil|last=Kaufman|url=https://assets.billboard.com/articles/columns/rock/9576363/twenty-one-pilots-scaled-and-icy-ivestream-show|title=Twenty One Pilots Climb to New Heights With On June 16, 2021, the duo announced the [[Takeover Tour]], during which they would spend a week in each city they visited, performing at small clubs as well as large venues. The tour began in [[Denver|Denver, Colorado]] in September 2021, and concluded in London on June 25, 2022.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Gil|last=Kaufman|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/twenty-one-pilots-takeover-tour-dates-2021-2022/|title=Twenty One Pilots Announce Club Dates & Arena Shows for 2021–2022 'Takeover Tour'|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=June 16, 2021|access-date=March 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210616162836/https://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/rock/9587982/twenty-one-pilots-takeover-tour-dates-2021-2022/|archive-date=June 16, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> On July 23, 2021, [[Half Alive (band)|Half Alive]] and Arrested Youth were announced as openers for the U.S. leg of the tour.<ref>{{cite web|first=Natalie|last=VonderHeide|url=https://huntleyvoice.com/33389/thevoice/twenty-one-pilots-takeover-tour-really-did-take-over/|title=Twenty One Pilots "Takeover Tour" Really Did Take Over|work=Huntley Voice|date=October 20, 2021|access-date=March 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230602125512/https://huntleyvoice.com/33389/thevoice/twenty-one-pilots-takeover-tour-really-did-take-over/|archive-date=June 2, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> On September 17, 2021, the duo held a virtual concert for the online video game ''[[Roblox]]''.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Jem|last=Aswad|url=https://variety.com/2021/digital/news/twenty-one-pilots-21-roblox-concert-experience-1235058749/|title=Twenty One Pilots to Stage Elaborate Roblox 'Concert Experience'|magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=September 8, 2021|access-date=March 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230326032400/https://variety.com/2021/digital/news/twenty-one-pilots-21-roblox-concert-experience-1235058749/|archive-date=March 26, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== 2024–present: ''Clancy'' and ''Breach'' ===
{{Main|Clancy (album)|Breach (Twenty One Pilots album)|l1 = ''Clancy'' (album)|l2 = ''Breach'' (Twenty One Pilots album)}}

On February 15, 2024, the cover art of ''Vessel'', ''Blurryface'', ''Trench'', and ''Scaled and Icy'' were updated to be partially covered in red tape on streaming platforms.<ref>{{cite web|first=Bee|last=Delores|url=https://www.dexerto.com/music/twenty-one-pilots-fans-convinced-comeback-is-imminent-after-red-tape-appears-on-albums-2536534/|title=Twenty One Pilots fans convinced comeback is imminent after red tape appears on albums|work=Dexerto|date=February 15, 2024|access-date=March 5, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240216135243/https://www.dexerto.com/music/twenty-one-pilots-fans-convinced-comeback-is-imminent-after-red-tape-appears-on-albums-2536534/|archive-date=February ==Artistry==
[[File:Twenty One Pilots - Southside Festival 2022 - IMG 6030 - 4.jpg|thumb|170px|left|Twenty One Pilots is known for their physically active performances.]]

The duo grew up in strict Christian households where they had to either conceal their [[pop punk]] and [[Hip hop music|hip hop]] albums from the censure of their parents, or find faith-friendly counterparts.<ref name="Wilson">{{cite magazine|first=Carl|last=Wilson|url=http://www.slate.com/articles/arts/music_box/2017/01/why_twenty_one_pilots_are_america_s_biggest_rock_band.html|title=The Mood Swing Vote|magazine=[[Slate (magazine)|Slate]]|date=January 24, 2017|access-date=February 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201228141009/https://slate.com/culture/2017/01/why-twenty-one-pilots-are-americas-biggest-rock-band.html|archive-date=December 28, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> Both still identify as Christians.<ref name="Wilson"/> According to Dun, "I'd hide albums like [[Green Day]]'s ''[[Dookie]]'' under my bed. They'd find a Christian alternative, like [[Relient K]], and make me listen to that."<ref name="BigNew"/> However, his parents eventually relaxed on rock music, even allowing Dun to assemble a live drum kit in their basement.<ref name="BigNew"/> Joseph's first favorite band was the Christian [[rap rock]] trio [[DC Talk]].<ref name="Wilson"/> He taught himself the piano by playing along to songs on the radio by artists like the Beatles and [[Celine Dion]].<ref name="BigNew"/>

* [[garage rock]],<ref name="Clancy"/>
